suggestion: Admit or reject the third-party price and snap corpus
options: (A) reject: stay official-only, and backtests stay impossible this season | (B) admit as a labelled second class for backtesting and residual reporting only, never as a model input | (C) admit fully, including model inputs
cost_to_try: a day of audit work, no money
what_it_unlocks: Unblocks REQ-01, REQ-19, REQ-55 and every gate that needs a settled sample (G1, G4, G7)
what_would_change_this_call: If the log's own provenance turns out to be an operator-scraped feed whose terms forbid redistribution, fall back to (A) and buy a licensed feed instead

suggestion: Make the price-snapshot store real by capturing before each kickoff
options: (A) manual screenshots (rejected: the brief forbids manual input) | (B) scheduled fetch of the official schedule plus a licensed odds API | (C) derive an internal consensus only and never publish a residual
cost_to_try: an API plan and a daily job
what_it_unlocks: Turns a fair line into a closing-line-value measurement
what_would_change_this_call: If no licensed feed is affordable, (C) plus the prospective escrow is the only honest leaderboard

suggestion: Capture the inactives and game books before building any replacement-depth feature
options: (A) the league's dated inactives article per slate | (B) official game books per club per game | (C) skip and keep the column blank
what_it_unlocks: Confirms who actually started; unlocks REQ-06, REQ-25, REQ-31 and the availability half of REQ-46
what_would_change_this_call: If game books are not redistributable, the inactives article alone still settles the started-or-not question

suggestion: Fix depth capture at the source instead of widening coverage
options: (A) 32-club verification pass with dates and hashes | (B) build on snap share where charts fail | (C) freeze the feature
what_it_unlocks: Removes the two known parsing failures and the Houston hole before any deficiency matrix is built on top
what_would_change_this_call: If more than 4 clubs publish no usable chart, switch to (B) under the S-01 ruling

suggestion: Version every availability row against the last roster event
options: (A) join depth and availability to the transactions register at build time | (B) manual review of contradictions | (C) ignore until the sweep is complete
what_it_unlocks: Makes the 13 known contradictions automatic instead of anecdotal, and re-checks them weekly
what_would_change_this_call: If the register proves unpinnable because of pagination, (A) degrades to (B) and the sweep becomes the real blocker

suggestion: Turn captures into a real snapshot service
options: (A) keep artifacts in git | (B) object store with lifecycle rules plus a freshness alert | (C) both: git for published tables, object store for raw
what_it_unlocks: Immutable history and a drift alert that fires when nobody is looking at the site
what_would_change_this_call: If the repo's artifact cap becomes the limit, (B) alone

suggestion: Consolidate the eight NFL desks under one index
options: (A) name one desk and mark the rest historical | (B) build one index over all eight with capture dates and coverage | (C) delete the older desks
what_it_unlocks: Stops the same requirement being answered eight different ways with eight different dates
what_would_change_this_call: If the desks disagree on a number, the index must show both rather than pick one, so (C) is only safe after a diff

suggestion: Calibrate designations before using them as a feature
options: (A) use the measured play-rate table as a prior | (B) refuse to use designations at all | (C) use them only as a filter on the schedule, never as a weight
what_it_unlocks: Replaces folklore percentages with measured rates and intervals (Out 0.0002 of 4001; Questionable 0.6180 of 4820)
what_would_change_this_call: If the third-party join is rejected outright, (B) is the honest answer and the feature stays unbuilt

suggestion: Score the week-11 registrations the moment the week settles
options: (A) automatically in CI | (B) manually at week's end (rejected: the brief forbids manual input) | (C) automatically with a printed report in the repo
what_it_unlocks: First real leaderboard numbers, with no leakage by construction
what_would_change_this_call: If a registered forecast is edited after kickoff, the run is void - the manifest hash is the check

suggestion: Keep both total estimators until a real retirement
options: (A) keep publishing both with the gap column | (B) collapse to the better of the six test weeks now
what_it_unlocks: Protects against a decision made on 78 games that reverses on 90
what_would_change_this_call: Collapsing now would be result-chasing: A wins 3 of 6 and B wins 3 of 6, and the league-average baseline beat both in 2 of 6

options: (A) publish everything including row-level captures | (B) derived analysis public and raw row-level private until the terms are read, as the brief states | (C) (B) with a documented exception list
what_it_unlocks: Removes the contradiction between the brief's rule and what is already public on this site
what_would_change_this_call: If you decide the captures are yours to publish, record that as the exception list rather than leaving pages inconsistent with each other

suggestion: Stop answering the same brief in parallel namespaces
options: (A) one session owns the brief and the rest take narrow, claimed tasks | (B) keep parallel desks | (C) (A) plus a claim file that makes the narrow task explicit
what_it_unlocks: Duplicates are how a wrong claim survived five desks unchallenged (see Q-07 on this desk's corrections page)
what_would_change_this_call: If parallel desks continue, each must publish a diff against the desk it replaced, or the duplication cost stays hidden
